business_keys.rationale: REQ-002 explicitly states the product number is unique and is the natural business key used day to day; REQ-001 requires unambiguous identification. Stable, unique, business-recognised.

System-generated surrogate in the operational system; REQ-055-3 says technical identifiers without business meaning should not surface in reporting. Weak business key, though used as FK in other sources.
REQ-004 states the product name is not guaranteed unique and must not be relied on to identify a product.
REQ-030 says a product category must be identifiable by its name (description); REQ-029 defines it as the top level of the hierarchy.
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-031 says a product subcategory must be identifiable by its name; it belongs to exactly one category (REQ-032).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-036 states the business must be able to identify a product model by its name; shared by several products (REQ-037).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).
REQ-044 states each culture is identified by a short culture code; this is a business-recognised, stable code (not a generated number).
REQ-093 states each unit of measure is identified by a short code; stable and business-recognised, used across quantity, size and weight (REQ-094).
REQ-001-2 states each manufacturing location is identified by a name (shop floors and work centres).
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-019-2 requires each work order to be uniquely identifiable; WorkOrderID is the only listed identifier, and the business raises and refers to work orders (REQ-018-2, REQ-007-3), though it is system-assigned.
REQ-026-2 says scrap reasons are a standard list each carrying a failure description; the name is the business-recognised value, though uniqueness is not explicitly stated.
System-generated surrogate; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-001-3 requires each inventory transaction to be identified uniquely; TransactionID is the only identifier, though system-generated. The same ID exists in live and archive stores (REQ-018-3, REQ-022-3).
REQ-024-3 requires identifying each review; no natural identifier is stated (reviewer name and e-mail are personal data, REQ-034-3), so the generated ID is the only option.
REQ-057 and REQ-058 describe illustrations without a natural identifier; the generated ID is the only identifying source column.
REQ-043 describes a library of free-text descriptions with no natural key; the generated ID is the only identifier.
REQ-049 describes a photograph library with no natural identifier stated; the generated ID is the only identifier.

REQ-060 requires identifying each document in the controlled library, and REQ-062 requires reconstructing the hierarchy; DocumentNode is the hierarchical position identifier. Title is not stated as unique.
System-generated GUID; weak business key (REQ-055-3).

REQ-068 and REQ-069 say each document carries an engineering change approval number and documents trace to the authorising change; recognised by the business, though the change object is not described further.

hubs.name: hub_product
hubs.description: Product master concept. Anchored on ProductID because it is the key carried by every product-related source (inventory, work orders, routing, transactions, reviews, history); the business-facing ProductNumber is held as a descriptive attribute.

hubs.name: hub_product_category
hubs.description: Top level of the merchandising hierarchy (bikes, components, clothing, accessories).

hubs.name: hub_product_subcategory
hubs.description: Second level of the product classification hierarchy.

hubs.name: hub_product_model
hubs.description: Product model shared by several products; holds design, catalogue and manufacturing instruction content.

hubs.name: hub_culture
hubs.description: Language/locale designation identified by a short culture code.

hubs.name: hub_unit_measure
hubs.description: Standard unit of measure identified by a short code, used for BOM quantities, size and weight.

hubs.name: hub_location
hubs.description: Manufacturing location / work centre that also holds inventory.

hubs.name: hub_work_order
hubs.description: Work order raised to manufacture a product.

hubs.name: hub_inventory_transaction
hubs.description: Inventory transaction, fed from both the live store and the archive so they form one continuous history.

hubs.name: hub_illustration
hubs.description: Technical illustration used in manufacturing instructions.

hubs.name: hub_product_description
hubs.description: Free-text marketing description in the description library.

hubs.name: hub_product_photo
hubs.description: Photograph in the product photograph library.

hubs.name: hub_document
hubs.description: Entry (folder or document) in the controlled document library, identified by its hierarchical node.
